title: How Two Android Intent Bugs Broke My App’s Red Alert Button
content_md: I'm building an Android app for my mother. She lives in a village; the rest of us live in cities, and I wanted a way for her to tell us how she's feeling without typing a word. The app is called CareVocal (internally, CareBridge). It has three big buttons: green for "feeling good", yellow for "something hurts", red for "need help". The red button is the one I can't get wrong. This is the story of the two times I did. What the red button is supposed to do One tap, and three things happen: The entry is saved and flagged for her doctor. A pre-filled SMS opens, addressed to her trusted contacts, with a fixed alert message and a timestamp. No location. I never collect it. The phone dialer opens with the local emergency number already typed in. She still has to tap "send" and tap "call". That's deliberate: no automatic dialing, and Google Play restricts apps that message people in the background. The app prepares everything, and a human confirms it. There's a rule I wrote down before I wrote any code: the alert never waits on anything slow. Not transcription, not the network, not the microphone. The person pressing it may be dizzy, frightened, or both. Bug 1: the dialer wins, the SMS vanishes I tested on my own phone. I tapped red. The dialer appeared. The SMS never did. My code did the obvious thing: context.startActivity(smsIntent) context.startActivity(dialIntent) Two intents, two apps, back to back.
